title: Sorting
hook: Sorting is elements physically finding their place — comparisons decide who swaps.

steps.caption: Compare neighbors. 7 and 2 are out of order, so they swap.

nodeCaptions.cursor: Different sorts pick different pairs, but the idea is compare → maybe swap/move.
nodeCaptions.a: After the swap this slot holds the smaller value.

steps.caption: Keep comparing until every element is in order.

nodeCaptions.c: When no more swaps are needed, the array is sorted.
nodeCaptions.b: Faster algorithms avoid obvious wasted comparisons — same goal, less work.

takeaways: Sorting rearranges by comparisons (or by counting/radix tricks).
Naive sorts are easy to see; better sorts reduce how many swaps you need.
Sorted data unlocks binary search and many other algorithms.

quiz.question: What is sorting doing, in one sentence?
choices: Rearranging elements into an agreed order
Moving the array to the GPU
quiz.explanation: Order is the product — algorithms differ in how they get there.
